record_body:
HubSpot Company Record — CrestaPay (crestapay.com)

Summary / why this is hot:
- High-intent evaluation. They’re actively benchmarking providers and asked for a “credible, reproducible” performance economics view (latency per $) broken down by region.
- Trigger: they saw internal chatter about our upcoming/public benchmark and want to use it to shortlist vendors for a Q2 rollout.

Current stage: Evaluation
Primary contacts (notes):
- Head of Platform Engineering (buyer): focused on throughput and reliability under burst.
- Procurement (influencer): wants cost predictability and a clean pricing narrative.
- Security (blocker): data handling + residency language must be explicit.

Use case / workload:
- Primary: LLM-powered support agent + ticket summarization (chat/completions w/ streaming).
- Secondary: internal knowledge base search (embeddings + retrieval).
- Traffic profile (their words): “spiky during business hours, then quieter overnight; concurrency jumps with incidents.”

Latency / throughput requirements:
- Chat:
  - Target p50 TTFT: < 400ms (streaming)
  - Target p95 end-to-end: < 2.5s for typical responses
  - Concurrency target: 150–300 concurrent requests during peak
- Embeddings:
  - Batch-friendly; they can queue but want predictable throughput for nightly backfills.
- Reliability:
  - Wants a defined fallback strategy (model variant + region) for capacity events.

Cost / unit economics:
- Very cost-sensitive. They’re measuring “cost per resolved ticket” and back-calculating acceptable $/1M tokens.
- Asked specifically for:
  - cost per 1M input/output tokens
  - latency/$ metric definition (how computed; whether includes warmups; how we handle variance)
  - region pricing differences and how that shows up in the numbers

Region / residency needs:
- Must support us-east for production.
- EU data residency is a hard requirement for a subset of enterprise customers (at minimum eu-west).
- Quote from call notes: “If you can’t show region-specific numbers and a clear residency posture, we can’t take this to the compliance committee.”

Deployment + product fit:
- Strong preference for VPC deployment (Redwood Private in VPC) for chat traffic.
- Open to Hosted API for dev/test and embeddings if residency story is clean.
- Interested in Dedicated capacity for predictable peak-hour performance (they’ve been burned by shared endpoint variance).

Security/compliance checklist (partial):
- SSO/SAML for console access
- Audit logs (API + admin actions)
- KMS integration / customer-managed keys
- Retention controls (request/response logging off by default; explicit configuration)
- Data residency statement (where prompts/completions are processed + stored)

Competitive notes:
- They are running side-by-side tests with Bedrock + at least one “OpenAI-compatible aggregator.”
- They distrust vendor benchmarks that hide variance. They asked how many runs, what window, and whether results are cherry-picked.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2025-02-03 — Inbound form fill: “Looking for low-latency inference with region controls; need numbers for US + EU.”
- 2025-02-06 — Intro call (Stephanie + Markus): gathered targets; they requested our benchmark methodology + tables.
- 2025-02-11 — Email follow-up: they asked for “latency per dollar” definition + whether caching/batching is enabled.
- 2025-02-14 — Markus sent technical notes on region routing headers + fallback patterns (OpenAI-compat header question).
- 2025-02-21 — Eval planning call: they agreed to review the public report internally if we provide (1) methodology FAQ, (2) region breakdown, (3) variance language.

What they asked for from the benchmark content:
- A public-facing report they can forward (PDF or landing page) with:
  - explicit methodology (workload distribution, concurrency, warmup/caching policy)
  - region-by-region results for US and EU
  - disclaimers/confidence/variance guidance (so it passes internal scrutiny)
- They do NOT need raw logs; they explicitly said “no raw logs needed, just defensible methodology.”

Next steps (owner plan):
1) Send the public benchmark landing page + PDF and highlight the sections they care about:
   - latency/$ definition
   - region table for us-east + eu-west
   - variance/re-run policy language
2) Offer a 45-min technical deep dive with Markus:
   - VPC deployment architecture + routing/fallback policy
   - how to reproduce a small slice of the benchmark against their prompts
3) If they confirm go-forward, propose 2-week guided eval:
   - Hosted API for quick integration
   - Dedicated/VPC path for production constraints

Internal notes / positioning:
- Lead with credibility: reproducibility + clear constraints, not “we’re always #1.”
- Tie the benchmark back to procurement language (predictable unit economics) AND engineering language (p95 + variance + routing).

Risks:
- If our published region coverage doesn’t include their preferred EU region naming, we need to map precisely (avoid confusion between eu-west vs eu-central).
- They will challenge any single-number headline; must be ready to talk confidence intervals and “it depends on workload.”

Owner: Stephanie Nguyen
SE: Markus Klein
